column4: Visit note | 2025-06-15 04:30 PM | Dr. Sharmin Akter, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Priya Paul, 27, female. Miss Paul presents to the clinic today reporting concerns regarding weight gain and acne. She mentions that she works as a fisherman, and she first noticed the weight gain after starting a desk job in Banani. She has a known history of Bronchial asthma. She denies any severe pelvic pain, abnormal bleeding patterns, or visual disturbances. On physical examination, her vital signs are as follows: BMI 32.8, BP 113/72 mmHg, pulse 87 bpm, and weight 45 kg. Abdominal examination is soft with no overt tenderness. Based on the clinical presentation and examination findings, our assessment is Polycystic ovary syndrome. Plan: tests ordered before starting treatment: a pelvic ultrasound and hormone profile; no new medicine was prescribed today. She was advised to aim for 5% weight loss, exercise 150 minutes a week, and reduce sugary drinks. Follow-up is scheduled for after the test results are ready.

Visit note | 2025-06-17 02:30 PM | Dr. Sharmin Akter, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Sabina Alam, 27, female. Ms. Alam visits the clinic complaining of painful cramps in the first days of each period and nausea with the pain. She is an NGO field officer who notes that her symptoms became worse since a stressful family move to Rajshahi. Her medical history includes Hypothyroidism. She denies heavy intermenstrual bleeding or systemic fever. Examination reveals a pain score 7/10, BP 122/86 mmHg, pulse 86 bpm, and weight 73 kg. Abdominal examination shows lower quadrant tenderness without peritoneal signs. Assessment: Primary dysmenorrhoea. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no medicine needed at this stage, and no new medicine was prescribed today. She was advised to use a hot water bottle, do light exercise, and keep a period diary. Follow-up is arranged in 3 months with the period diary.

Visit note | 2025-06-17 04:30 PM | Dr. Imran Kabir, Gastroenterology | Patient: Shathi Sikder, 72, female. Mrs. Sikder reports experiencing a sour taste in the mouth, symptoms worse when lying down, and burning behind the breastbone after meals. She works as a retired civil servant and states that her discomfort got worse after weeks of fried snacks at tea stalls in Barishal. She has no significant chronic comorbidities. She denies dysphagia, unintended weight loss, or vomiting blood. Examination findings show BMI 29.4, BP 116/70 mmHg, pulse 73 bpm, and weight 82 kg. Abdominal examination reveals mild epigastric tenderness. Assessment: Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no medicine needed at this stage, and no new medicine was prescribed today. She was advised to eat smaller meals, avoid oily and spicy food late at night, and raise the head of the bed. Follow-up is set for 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-06-21 10:00 AM | Dr. Shamima Nasrin, Ophthalmology | Patient: Sumaiya Molla, 75, female. Mrs. Molla attends the clinic complaining of symptoms worse in air conditioning, gritty burning eyes, and long hours of screen time. She works as a madrasa teacher and notes her issues became worse since moving to a new air-conditioned office in Dhanmondi. She has a history of Type 2 diabetes mellitus. She denies sudden visual loss, eye discharge, or severe ocular pain. Examination records show tear break-up time 4 seconds, BP 133/83 mmHg, pulse 91 bpm, and weight 56 kg. Ocular examination confirms mild conjunctival injection bilaterally. Assessment: Dry eye syndrome. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no medicine needed at this stage, and no new medicine was prescribed today. She was advised to look away from the screen every 20 minutes, blink often, and use a humidifier. Follow-up is scheduled for 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-06-21 11:00 AM | Dr. Moinul Haque, Neurology | Patient: Dalia Khan, 79, female. Mrs. Khan comes in describing tingling like pins and needles and burning in both feet. She works as a shopkeeper and noticed these sensations after long hours standing at a factory in Mirpur. She reports no major chronic medical conditions. She denies muscle weakness, gait instability, or back pain. Examination demonstrates reduced sensation at 3 of 10 monofilament test sites, BP 129/83 mmHg, pulse 69 bpm, and weight 86 kg. Cranial nerves are intact. Assessment: Peripheral neuropathy. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no medicine needed at this stage, and no new medicine was prescribed today. She was advised to check the feet daily for cuts, wear soft closed shoes, and keep blood sugar under control. Follow-up is planned in 6 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-06-23 11:00 AM | Dr. Selina Parvin, Neurology | Patient: Ayesha Khan, 66, female. Mrs. Khan comes to the clinic stating she experiences symptoms worse at night, numbness in the toes, and burning in both feet. She is a homemaker and states her trouble started after years of high sugar found at a health camp in Cox's Bazar. She has no known chronic illnesses. She denies active foot ulcers, bowel or bladder incontinence, or major motor weakness. Examination findings include reduced sensation at 7 of 10 monofilament test sites, BP 117/74 mmHg, pulse 92 bpm, and weight 90 kg. Deep tendon reflexes are sluggish. Assessment: Peripheral neuropathy. Plan: tests ordered before starting treatment: HbA1c, vitamin B12, and a nerve conduction study; no new medicine was prescribed today. She was advised to check the feet daily for cuts, wear soft closed shoes, and keep blood sugar under control. Follow-up is arranged for after the test results are ready.

Visit note | 2025-06-25 03:30 PM | Dr. Mahbuba Rahman, Psychiatry | Patient: Kawsar Dewan, 30, male. Mr. Dewan attends for review reporting persistent low mood, no interest in usual activities, and low energy. He works as a pharmacist and states his symptoms began after losing a job in Rangpur. He has no other medical comorbidity. He reports taking his previous care plan seriously. The patient denies thoughts of self-harm, and a safety plan with the emergency number 999 was discussed. On mental state examination, he is alert and cooperative with blunted affect. Vitals recorded: PHQ-9 score 15, BP 111/83 mmHg, pulse 81 bpm, weight 94 kg. Assessment: Depressive episode. Plan: chronic follow-up: continue current medicines, no new prescription issued, and no new medicine was prescribed today. He was advised to keep a daily routine, walk outdoors daily, start counselling sessions, and call 999 or come to the clinic at once if thoughts of self-harm appear. Follow-up is set in 2 weeks.
